title: What If Every Fungus on Earth Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every fungus on Earth vanished? Not just mushrooms, all of them. Forests would starve.
Scientists have named about one hundred forty-four thousand species, out of an estimated two to four million.
About ninety percent of plant species depend on fungi at their roots to reach nutrients.
Orchids couldn't even germinate, because every orchid relies on fungi to start and survive.
Fungi are also the main organisms that break down cellulose and lignin, the tough material in wood and leaves. Dead plants would pile up.
Nearly everything on land would starve or smother. And only about five percent of fungal species have even been named.
